recipes.name: Chef John’s Cioppino
ingredients_raw: 0.5 teaspoon red pepper flakes, or to taste
1 Dungeness crab, cleaned, cooked, and cracked
1 pound medium raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Combine butter and olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-low heat. Stir in onion and celery with a pinch of salt; cook until onion is soft and golden, 6 to 7 minutes. Stir in garlic and cook for 1 minute.

Stir wine into onion mixture; increase heat to high and bring to a simmer. Stir in tomato puree, water, bay leaf, oregano, red pepper flakes, and Worcestershire sauce. Reduce heat to low and simmer for about 35 minutes.
Increase heat to high and bring mixture to a boil. Stir in lemon and cod, then return to a simmer for about 2 minutes.
Stir in crab, shrimp, and mussels. Cover and simmer until mussels are cooked and open, about 5 minutes.
Stir in fresh parsley and basil; season with salt and pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John’s Cioppino
raw_recipe.description: This cioppino recipe is a version of San Francisco’s famous dish that has it all. A tangy, spicy broth featuring shrimp, mussels, cod, and Dungeness crab.

review.reviewBody: I made the broth exactly as directed except I forgot the bay leaf. I added the seafood that is available in Baltimore in October..... little neck clams, snow crabs, grouper, mussels and bay scallops. It was very simple but very elegant and tasted like a high priced restaurant cioppino!!! The lemon is a must but a couple of slices goes a long way. I did add some chili oil in addition to the red pepper flakes to wake it up. I have made many cioppino recipes and this was my favorite by far! Crusty sourdough bread is required by law.

A new go to recipe. Used puree tomatoes & diced tomatoes (canned with basil and thyme), tilapia, fresh clams, shrimp with heads on (heads add unique flavor). Left out crab for fear it would over power other ingredients. Simmered tomato sauce for two hours, let cool and then re-heated adding seafood. Recommend adding clams first since they take longer to open. Allow 3-4 minutes with calms only, then add shrimp (wait one minute) and then add fish last. I seasoned the fish with salt and pepper before adding. Cook 3-4 minutes after fish added. Turn off heat, remove shrimp, peel for your guest (messy and hot). Temperature of soup will be perfect by the time you have peeled shrimp and cooled your fingers. Return shrimp to soup. Serve over fresh linguini (yum). Serve with warm sour dough bread. The longer tomato sauce simmer and reheat thickens to stew consistency and allows the sauce to stick to the noodles. You could serve over rice or simply as a stew and dip bread. Glad I discovered this new dish!!!

This is my Christmas Eve dish. I sometimes vary the type of fish and seafood, and usually use clam stock (from canned clams) instead of water, but otherwise follow this precisely. I have diced up a potato on occasion to add in with the celery and onion. The real trick is to let that broth simmer to absorb the flavours. And add the seafood only at the end so it doesn’t go tough and rubbery.? by making this only once a year, it is a special treat on a cool Christmas Eve. ?Outstanding with a crusty baguette and fresh butter.

Tasty! I did make some additions/substitutions. That’s the wonderful thing about soup-adaptability! Used all olive oil, no butter Extra onions, red and yellow 1 & 1/2 green bell pepper (because I had it) Subbed unsalted chicken stock for water Doubled cooking spices; added tbsp paprika Subbed diced tomatoes Used frozen seafood mix from Aldi - follow thawing/cooking time on package (chop up thawed seafood as desired). Will definitely try it again with fresh seafood when it’s in season!

Delicious light tomato sauce. I made this with mussels, little necks, cod and shrimp. Dungeness crab was not available. this cries out to be served with linguine NOT rice. Super flavor. you won't be disappointed.

This was behind delicious and very simple to make. I do the feast of the seven fishes every Christmas Eve and it's hard to pull it al together with so many different dishes going a once. I decided to go easy on myself this year and put four of the fishes into this stew (my family won't let me get rid of the lobster, crab legs or calamari). I ended up using shrimp, white fish, clams and muscles but you could literally use anything you want. I will cut back on the cayenne even more as it was very spicy with even half of the suggested amount. Other than that this was wonderful and I will make it again next year.

Yes I tried it as written, but I did do one little tweak to it. I shaved 5 slices from a bulb of fennel(anise)and added the slices just before the 35 minute cook time. I had fennel in cioppino in Fort Collins, Co. and it was the best I ever had! This is a close second!

My first attempt and my husband said I should make this every weekend! He loved it! Made for my friends last weekend and they gave me a 10/10! 

Some substitutes: I used fennel instead of celery; boil the prawn shells & heads to get the 2 cups of water. 
Had the stew with sourdough baguette toasted with gremolata butter, and paired with Riesling wine. Superb!

Thanks Chef John! Your recipe is easy to follow and gives me confidence to cook again!
Excellent and easy recipe. I used chicken stock instead of water, added clam juice and 1 teaspoon sugar. My husband loved it. Will make again and again!

This cioppino recipe was so great and simple to follow! I made it and used more mussels since our market had a smaller selection. I also didn’t have white wine but had a good dry rosé and it worked great!

It was tough to make a recipe and stick to it, but I only made very small changes to this one. Instead of water I used chicken broth, but only because I needed to use it before it went bad. I also skipped the Dungeness crab, as I wasn't sure how to clean it and wanted to keep things simpler for myself. 

That being said, this recipe was awesome. Very flavorful and perfect with the fresh baked bread I served it with. 

I'm fairly sure that the person who said it was too sweet must have used a sweet wine (like a moscato or white Zinfandel), as mine wasn't sweet at all. I used the same Sauvignon blanc that I drink regularly and it turned out great. Not sweet at all. 

I couldn't find tomato purée at my grocery store, so I bought the tomato sauce that that didn't have any other ingredients than tomato purée and water. Be careful, though. Most tomato sauces had all kinds of extra seasoning added. Read the labels!

This was my first time working with live mussels. Make sure you clean the outside of the shells and the easiest way to de-beard them is to use a paring knife to pull the beard against your finger and up out of the shell. Also, if you have any mussels in your bunch that are open and won't close back up that probably means the mussel is dead and you want to discard it. 

My only regret was that I didn't make a seafood stock from the shrimp I peeled (I bought large shell-on deveined shrimp) to add in place of the chicken stock I used out of necessity. 

Very good.
I used halibut and shrimp (no mussels or crab). They were dynamite on their own. Too much lemon for me. Will make this again with half the lemon.
We enjoy mussels occasionally and this is my go to recipe.
This could have been good if made with chopped tomatoes instead of tomatoe pureee. Ended up more of a tonatoe seafood soup than a true ciopinno
Very good, easy to make. I added Dungeness crab, so even better.

I used fish stock instead of water, fire roasted dice tomatoes and ran them thru the food processor and half of tomato paste, in addition to mussels and shrimp, I added clams, crab meat, scallops, used sole fish instead. recipe had ingredients list cut off so I calculated basil and parsley, 2 spoonfuls each, chopped it. amazing flavors. my husband and I loved this dish. will cook it again.
